TORONTO, ON / ACCESS Newswire / November 14, 2026 /
Gabriel Resources Ltd.
Gabriel
" or the "
Company
") announces that the ad hoc committee (the "
Annulment
Committee
") of the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes ("
ICSID
") has dismissed the application by Gabriel and its wholly owned subsidiary, Gabriel Resources (Jersey) Limited ("
Gabriel Jersey
"), to annul the arbitral award dated March 8, 2024 (the "
Award
") in their proceedings against Romania (ICSID Case No. ARB/15/31) (the "
Annulment Application
The Award, which dismissed Gabriel's claims against Romania by a two-to-one majority, therefore remains in force, including the order (the "
Costs Order
") requiring the Company and Gabriel Jersey to pay approximately US$10 million of Romania's costs, together with interest.

The Annulment Committee rejected all five grounds on which Gabriel had sought annulment of the Award. It found that the Tribunal was properly constituted, that the arbitrator appointed by Romania was not required to disclose the matters Gabriel had raised, and that the majority of the Tribunal had applied the applicable law, respected Gabriel's procedural rights and stated adequate reasons for its decision.

The Annulment Committee directed Gabriel and Romania to share equally the fees and expenses of the Committee and ICSID, with each side bearing its own legal fees and expenses. As Gabriel had advanced the costs of the proceedings, the Committee ordered Romania to reimburse Gabriel approximately US$211,000. The Committee awarded no interest on that amount and set no payment deadline.

The decision has material implications for Gabriel's financial position and ability to continue as a going concern. The Company has limited liquidity and requires additional funding to meet its obligations, including the Costs Order and outstanding legal fees.
As of the date of this release, US$894,365 in subscription proceeds remain outstanding under the Company's US$3.4 million private placement (the "
Offering

"), as described in its news release dated November 9, 2026. The TSX Venture Exchange's current deadline for completing the Offering is November 16, 2026. The Company will provide a further update on the status of the Offering.

The Board is reviewing the Company's position with its legal and financial advisers. That review includes the availability of further funding, the potential value of the remaining assets and licence-related interests in Romania of the Company and its subsidiaries (collectively, the "
Group
"), and whether any viable restructuring or other alternative is available.

There can be no assurance that further funding or a viable alternative will be available. If no such funding or alternative is available, the Company may be required to commence proceedings under applicable insolvency legislation, in which case holders of the Company's common shares would be unlikely to receive any recovery. In that event, the TSX Venture Exchange ("
TSXV
") could suspend trading in and delist the Company's common shares, or transfer the Company's listing to NEX.

In light of these risks, investors are urged to exercise caution when trading in the Company's common shares. The Company will provide a further update as soon as the Board has determined the appropriate next steps.
Anna El-Erian, Chair of the Board, commented:

We are deeply disappointed by the decision. We thank our shareholders for their support throughout these proceedings. The Board is now focused on assessing the implications for the Group and determining the appropriate next steps in light of its financial position and obligations.

About Gabriel

Gabriel Resources Ltd. is a Canadian resource company listed on the TSX Venture Exchange under the symbol GBU. Following the dismissal of the Annulment Application, the Company is assessing its financial position and the options available in respect of its remaining assets and interests in Romania.
Gabriel holds an 80.69% interest in Roșia Montană Gold Corporation S.A. ("
RMGC

"), with the remaining 19.31% held by Minvest Roșia Montană S.A., a Romanian state-owned company. RMGC holds the Company's interests in the Roșia Montană gold and silver project. In June 2024, the competent Romanian authority rejected RMGC's application to extend the project's exploitation licence. RMGC is challenging that refusal before the Romanian courts.
